contract: Reviewed performance diagnostics after deterministic allocation cleanup

ruleDecisions.rationale: Explicit default initializers are concentrated in legacy/result/property models and two line value fields. No material runtime benefit was established, while the initializer communicates the intended default.
Sixty-one members are public instance contracts whose conversion to static is breaking. Seven are private but lack hot-path evidence for a material static-dispatch benefit.
All 32 zero-length allocations use Array.Empty<T>(), removing a deterministic allocation without changing declared API shape or element mutability.
All nine single-task Task.WaitAll calls use Task.Wait(), avoiding the params array while preserving blocking and AggregateException behavior.
The eleven concrete-type suggestions affect setup, collection construction, smoke, or report parsing paths; no measured dispatch bottleneck justifies tighter local contracts.
All 82 sites are one-shot smoke or benchmark arguments. Hoisting non-empty arrays would add shared mutable state without product runtime benefit.
The sole JsonSerializerOptions instance is created once for final benchmark report output, so caching provides no repeated-use benefit.
